ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0071 records that Providence's constitutional design has not had legal review, which is why the restored governance chapters are kept in proposal grammar throughout. CTD-0075 forbids attributing a named recurring apparatus to Volume III, which changed the chapter references in this part from named sections to named arguments. CTD-0006 requires that no physiological evidence determine governance standing, which bears on the stewardship chapters. CTD-0055 requires unimplemented safeguards to read as requirements. CTD-0007 governs the self-epigraphs, which keep the Adapted from attribution.

findings.summary: The six named capture risks were removed.

evidence.baseline: It named the general categories of capture risk, political capture, corporate capture, charismatic capture, ideological capture, financial capture, and technological capture, and identified the constitutional commitment to designing against each of them.

findings.diagnosis: The chapter develops three of the six. Naming all six is what tells the reader that three are not developed, which is an honest disclosure the shipped version removes. Charismatic capture in particular is named nowhere else in the volume despite being the risk the founder capture section circles.

findings.summary: The chapter's statement about the standing of its own proposals was deleted.

evidence.baseline: The proposed designs are not final. They are the best current judgments, informed by the historical record of analogous institutions and by the constitutional principles established in Volume III. They will need to be refined through the experience of the founding community.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and CTD-0055 read onto safeguard claims.
findings.diagnosis: CTD-0055 requires unimplemented safeguards to be stated as requirements rather than facts. This paragraph does exactly that, in the baseline, for the whole chapter. Removing it left the chapter's mechanisms asserted with no statement of their standing, which is the opposite of what the item asks for.

debtImpact.note: The restored paragraph states the chapter's safeguards as current judgments requiring refinement, which is the form the item asks for and which the shipped chapter had lost.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Three em dashes. Two were parenthetical appositives listing capture categories and became comma pairs. One in the epigraph separated two movements and became a period.
The shipped heading Founders, Funders, and Technical Dependence, which holds the route and names the three risks the chapter actually develops.
The six capture categories, the chapter's account of its own difficulty, and the standing of its proposals.

openQuestions: The chapter names six capture risks and develops three. Whether the other three belong here, elsewhere, or nowhere is a structural decision for the author. The shipped heading resolves it by naming only the three, which is honest and also hides the omission.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

The heading is the shipped one, not the baseline's. Baseline headings were not restored because `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records the rename and resolves the historical route, and this pass has no standing to add lineage entries. Where the baseline heading names the section better, that is recorded in the finding and left for the author.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The instructive case is a paragraph whose removal made a ledger item worse: CTD-0055 wants safeguards stated as requirements, and the baseline paragraph that did so for the whole chapter was cut. A paydown can be undone by compression elsewhere without anyone touching the item.
